- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., post-75+ values), then fail to correct downward.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods — when history shows consolidation or decline, forecast still holds upward bias.
- Forecast lags in capturing recent downward momentum; true values often dip below forecast after 10–15 days.
- In high-volatility periods (e.g., 2025-01), model overreacts to recent spikes, leading to exaggerated upward bias.
- Model consistently underestimates the true mean of the 30-day history, especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late or too much.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model fails to reflect it until later days (lagged correction).
- Model overfits recent high values, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
- In cases of sustained upward momentum, model forecasts peak too early and then overcorrects downward — creating false troughs.
